# Lemma 4.3: Decomposition of the RL Gradient Interference

Lemma 4.3 (p. 5) states:

$$\mathcal{I}_{\text{RL}}(i,j)=\mathbb{E}_{x,x'}\left[\frac{1}{G^{2}}\sum_{k=1}^{G}\sum_{l=1}^{G}\hat{A}_{i,k}(x)\,\hat{A}_{j,l}(x')\,\langle\delta S_{i,k}(x),\,\delta S_{j,l}(x')\rangle\right]$$

## The pieces

- **Normalising factor:** $\frac{1}{G^{2}}$. This is the product of the two $\frac{1}{G}$ averaging factors, one from each task's GRPO gradient estimate (Def. 4.2, Eq. 3; Eq. 6, p. 5).
- **Sums:** a double sum. The index $k$ runs over task $i$'s $G$ rollouts for input $x$, and $l$ runs over task $j$'s $G$ rollouts for input $x'$ (p. 5).
- **What multiplies the inner product:** the product of the two standardised advantages, $\hat{A}_{i,k}(x)\,\hat{A}_{j,l}(x')$. Each advantage is $\hat{A}_{i,k}=(r_{i,k}-\mu_{r_i}(x))/\sigma_{r_i}(x)$ (p. 5).
- **The inner product itself:** it is taken between residual score functions, not raw ones. The terms are:
  - Score function: $S_{i,k}(x)=\nabla_\theta\log\pi_\theta(y_k|x)$
  - Mean score: $\bar{S}_i(x)=\frac{1}{G}\sum_k S_{i,k}(x)$
  - Residual: $\delta S_{i,k}(x)=S_{i,k}(x)-\bar{S}_i(x)$ (p. 5)
- **Outer expectation:** taken over $x\sim\mathcal{D}_i$ and $x'\sim\mathcal{D}_j$ (Appendix C.1, p. 15).

## Why the mean term disappears

The decomposition relies on the zero-sum property of GRPO advantages, $\sum_{k=1}^{G}\hat{A}_{i,k}(x)=0$ (Eq. 4, p. 5).

The proof (Appendix C.1, p. 15) substitutes $S_{i,k}=\bar{S}_i+\delta S_{i,k}$ into the gradient sum:

$$\sum_k \hat{A}_{i,k}(\bar{S}_i+\delta S_{i,k}) = \bar{S}_i\underbrace{\sum_k\hat{A}_{i,k}}_{=0}+\sum_k\hat{A}_{i,k}\delta S_{i,k}$$

The mean direction $\bar{S}_i$ therefore cancels. Applying the same step to task $j$ and expanding the inner product gives the lemma.

The paper interprets this as the advantage function acting as a filter. It "algebraically removes the contribution of the mean gradient direction," so interference depends only on intra-group residuals. By contrast, SFT interference depends directly on $\langle S_i^*(x), S_j^*(x')\rangle$ (p. 5).
